problem: Find the values of $x$ for which the function $f(x)={e}^{2{x}^{2}-6x+3}$ is strictly decreasing.

feedback.problem:
Given that $g(x)=3{x}^{4}-8{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+1$ is defined for $x\in (-8,8),$ find the values of $x$ for which the function is strictly decreasing.

$x\in (${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The function is strictly decreasing where ${g}^{′}(x)<0.$ Differentiating $g(x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =12{x}^{3}-24{x}^{2}+12x \\  & =12x({x}^{2}-2x+1) \\  & =12x{(x-1)}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

so we need to solve the inequality

$$
12x{(x-1)}^{2}<0.
$$

Since $(x-1)^{2}\ge 0$ for all real $x$, the sign of $12x{(x-1)}^{2}$ is determined by the sign of $12x$, so $12x{(x-1)}^{2}<0$ exactly when $12x<0.$ This yields

$$
\begin{aligned}12x & <0 \\ x & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the function is restricted to $x\in (-8,8),$ we conclude that $g(x)$ is strictly decreasing on the interval $x\in (-8,0).$
